title.narrative: Enhancing Nutrition Prevention and Support for Drought-Affected Populations in Qansax Dheere District, Bay Region

description.narrative: ltpgtKRDO proposed an integrated nutrition project in Qansax Dheere district, targeting drought-affected populations and focusing on the prevention and treatment of acute malnutrition among children under five, as well as pregnant and breastfeeding women. The project will concentrate on two core components: Maternal, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN), and the Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM). Implementation will follow a hybrid approach, combining community-based interventions with facility-based nutrition services. One fixed Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) site will be established at Towfiiq Health Facility, supported by five outreach sites in Shiidoley, Osmael,ltbrgtAl.amen IDP , Aabay, and Tiirkii villages. KRDO will manage screening, identification, and treatment of uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition (SAM) cases at these sites, while referring complicated SAM and moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) cases to stabilization centers and TSFP sites run by partner organizations. A total of 17 trained nutrition personnel—including 11 facility-based staff and 6 Community Health Workers (CHWs)—will be deployed under the supervision of the Nutrition Project Manager and with technical support from the Nutrition Cluster. Capacity building will be a cornerstone of the project, with all 17 staff trained on IMAM and MIYCN protocols. The training will also incorporate key cross-cutting themes including Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), Gender-Based Violence (GBV) mitigation and referral pathways, Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), and child protection. CHWs will further be trained to support family MUAC screening, IYCF messaging, and follow-up care, while also ensuring protection principles are upheld during community engagements.ltbrgtSocial and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) efforts will be driven through the formation and support of 60 care groups—10 per village across the six target locations. These groups will lead 120 cooking demonstrations, promoting the preparation of nutrient-rich porridge using the Tom Brown approach and advancing the "One Egg Per Day" campaign. Both initiatives are designed to improve household dietary diversity and child nutrition. In addition, care groups will work to address breastfeeding challenges and increase adoption of optimal MIYCN practices among caregivers.ltbrgtKRDO will ensure the inclusion of minority and other vulnerable populations through targeted mapping and the development of tailored strategies to address their specific needs. Representative committees for minority groups and persons with disabilities (PWDs) will be formed to monitor and report cases of exclusion. Feedback and accountability mechanisms—including suggestion boxes, help desks, and community forums—will be made accessible in inclusive formats and languages. Data will be disaggregated to monitor representation, and minority staff will be actively recruited to foster inclusive programming and community ownership.ltbrgtCoordination with the Nutrition Cluster, protection and GBV actors, community health and WASH partners, and area-based coordination groups will be strengthened to ensure streamlined service delivery and effective referrals. Nutrition commodities such as Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTF) and essential supplies will be sourced from UNICEF and the Ministry of Health.ltbrgtAll monitoring and evaluation activities will employ Nutrition Cluster–approved tools, with mass screening data collected using Kobo Toolbox. Community engagement efforts will also include the development of formal agreements between KRDO and community gatekeepers in each village, incorporating PSEA clauses to uphold ethical standards and ensure accountability. These interventions will be aimed at to empowering the community, promote inclusive service delivery, and improve the nutritional status and resilience of vulnerable populations in Qansax Dheere.ltbrgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
